subject: Post-call recap: DPA & data handling clarifications - Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: DPA & data handling clarifications - Acme Payments

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great to learn more about Acme Payments' integration patterns and the data handling requirements you run into. Quick recap and next steps from our end: 

Summary of items you asked about:
- Controller vs. Processor: confirmation that Acme will be the Controller and Redwood will act as Processor for any customer data sent to our inference endpoints.
- Subprocessors: you asked for a current list of subprocessors and our process for adding them.
- Breach notification: you want contractual commitment for notification timing and remediation coordination.
- Data residency: EU residency for payment data and ability to restrict processing to an EU region.
- Retention & logging controls: how long we retain request/response logs, and what can be turned off/trimmed for PII.

Next steps I promised:
1) Send our current DPA and subprocessor list for review (attached).
2) Confirm controller/processor language and breach-notice timing; loop in security/legal for precise wording.
3) Share SOC 2 artifacts under NDA if helpful.
4) If the DPA needs redlines, happy to coordinate with your counsel.

I attached our standard DPA and the current subprocessor list. Ben (cc'd) will loop in Security/Legal to confirm breach and retention language and to surface any operational knobs we can offer (e.g., configurable log retention, redaction options, region pinning).

Would you prefer a short follow-up call tomorrow to go through the DPA or shall we handle via email?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (stub), subprocessor_list_20270419.csv (stub)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: DPA & data handling clarifications - Acme Payments

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap. A few clarifying asks from our legal/compliance team: 

- Please confirm in the DPA that Acme is Controller and Redwood is Processor.
- Can you provide an up-to-date subprocessor list and commit to notice before adding any new subprocessor that will process EU customer data?
- We request a contractually bound breach notification window of 72 hours after discovery. Is that acceptable?
- For PII and payment-related fields, can we restrict logging (or ensure redaction) and limit request/response retention to a configurable window (we prefer 90 days)?
- EU data residency: we need assurance that production processing for EU cardholder data will be pinned to an EU region.

If you can confirm these points and share the SOC 2 report under NDA, we can move to legal review. A quick 30-min follow-up tomorrow morning works if you have availability.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations, Acme Payments
alex.johnson@acme-payments.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme DPA asks - can Legal/Security confirm?

Marissa - looping you in (and Neha/Stephanie) to get precise language we should send back to Alex. Key asks to address: Processor/Controller clarification, 72-hour breach notice, subprocessor notice process, configurable log retention (90 days default), and EU region pinning for production.

I attached the DPA and current subprocessor csv per Marissa's note. Can Security confirm whether we can provide a contractual 72-hour notification commitment and whether we need any additional operational caveats (e.g., time-to-remediation SLA)? Legal - can you confirm whether the standard DPA language can be amended to explicitly state Acme as Controller and Redwood as Processor (we normally do) and whether we're open to notice-before-add for EU-impacting subprocessors?

Related: HubSpot deal RWI-8421 link below - please update once we have a proposed response. Need a reply to Acme by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (stub), subprocessor_list_20270419.csv (stub)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/8421

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: DPA & data handling clarifications - Acme Payments

Hi Alex - thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and next steps: 

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed - Acme Payments will be the Controller; Redwood will act as Processor. We will add an explicit clause in the DPA to reflect that role assignment for clarity.

2) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list_20270419.csv). For EU-impacting subprocessors we will commit to 30 days' notice before onboarding; for other subprocessors we provide notice and the option to object within 14 days. If you need stricter notice for EU-cardholder data, we can discuss contract-specific notice language.

3) Breach notification: We can commit to commercially reasonable efforts to notify you within 72 hours of discovery for incidents materially affecting Acme data, and to provide regular updates during remediation. Legal has suggested including standard caveats around investigation time and law enforcement constraints; if Acme requires a strict 72-hour unconditional SLA, please flag and we can escalate to leadership.

4) Retention & logging controls: Our default retention for request/response logs is 90 days. We offer configuration to reduce retention and to enable redaction of specific fields (e.g., PANs, SSNs). We can scope options in the DPA and operational runbook so your engineers can opt for minimal retention for sensitive fields.

5) Data residency: We support region pinning. For EU cardholder production traffic we can provision processing in our EU region; we will include a clause in the DPA committing to regional processing as part of the production environment setup and acceptance criteria.

6) SOC 2: We can share our SOC 2 Type II summary under NDA; attached is a high-level summary. If you want the full report, we can get it to you after an NDA is in place.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (stub), subprocessor_list_20270419.csv (stub), SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf (stub)

Proposed next steps:
- If this aligns, please confirm whether Acme will propose redlines to the attached DPA or prefer we send a slightly edited DPA with the explicit Processor/Controller language and the retention/residency commitments.
- We can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through any redlines or technical controls.

Happy to jump on a call - available 11:00-12:00 PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183
